2242cfd03e2e30928fe0.text: As a learner, making generalization is one of the skills you need to learn. It is

2c61369cbf1fe396ebe0.text: to support you to have a thorough understanding of any texts you will read. You will use this skill whenever you will be asked to have a simple summary of the text, to have a movie review, writing a synopsis of a play, and the like.

795d541a26315fbf0d96.text: More importantly, it will be useful in your everyday life setting especially in

2b612ad68e7ed91f37d7.text: dealing with what you know about the unchanging values in an unchanging world.

b44e6cbbcb7a2750f9e8.text: This module is design for you to help you be equipped with this skill. In this

652e35a7500b1441cf2d.text: module, you are expected to: a. Define what are generalizations; b. Differentiate invalid/faulty from valid/true generalizations; c. Recognize signal/clue words to use in making generalizations; and Make valid/true generalizations.

758c195f136985b99848.text: Generalization is a written or a spoken statement in which you say or write

564eb6a2213d124523b3.text: that something is true to all the time when it is only true to some of the time.

f5accedaf3b0f0cbb8e6.text: Some generalizations are valid or true and some are faulty or invalid. Valid

776079546ffc62084389.text: generalization means true. It is supported by facts, agreed with what has been already known, used logic and reasoning, and proven with several examples. On the other hand, faulty generalization means false or invalid, which is not supported by facts and usually use these key words: none, all, always, never, everyone, and nobody.

fc3b80fab0d223aa83ac.text: There are some words that signal or give us a clue to recognize

d90063c9a34fe791d797.text: generalizations. These are: sometimes, always, never most, many, all, generally, seldom, and none.

rows: Some people like to have chocolate as their favorite dessert.

All cats have brown fur. Some cats have brown fur.

aa715337bcb6c93a154a.text: people or things. Often, generalizations are not completely true, because there are examples of situations wherein the generalization does not apply. In this respect, generalizations can be compared to stereotypes that are sometimes offensive.
